processes.description: Arthur Andersen auditors send requests for their periodic testing (monthly gas testing, quarter-end P&L top sheets, MTM mini-book valuations, deal tickets and confirmations, index choices). Darron Giron receives them, forwards each to the desk or person who holds the support, collects what comes back and passes it to the auditors, chasing when replies lag. He also keeps a matrix of all requests made in a quarter and redirects requests for other desks, such as West desk work to Pat Ryder.
steps: Auditors send a request listing deals, books or figures they want support for.
The coordinator forwards the request to the trader, desk or risk contact who holds the data.
The contact pulls deal tickets, confirmations, valuations or P&L top sheets.
The coordinator chases contacts whose replies are late or asks who else can help.
Support is passed to the auditors, with explanations of differences where needed.
Open and closed requests are tracked in a request matrix for the quarter.

stalls.summary: Requests forwarded to desks sit unanswered and have to be chased more than once for status, sometimes days apart on the same request.
The right contact is not always known, so the request is bounced back asking who else can direct the auditors, while the coordinator is travelling and auditors press for answers.
Information gathered for the auditors gets misplaced and has to be requested again.

contradictions.summary: Different people are named as the one who handles West desk audit questions: one message sends West desk requests to Pat Ryder, another says West Hourly deals are researched by Kate Symes.

automation.approach: Keep a shared request log, built from the quarterly matrix, that records each auditor item, the desk owner, the date sent and the date answered, and flags overdue items for follow-up. Standard extracts of deal tickets, confirmations and P&L top sheets by deal number would cut the manual lookup each desk does.
automation.rationale: The work already revolves around a request matrix and repeated chasing; a structured tracker with owner by desk and status removes the guesswork over who holds the data and makes overdue items visible without manual status emails.

work_estimate.rationale: Each round requires someone on the desk to look up deal tickets, confirmations, valuations or P&L top sheets for a list of deals and assemble them, plus the coordinator updating the request matrix and explaining differences. Simple single-deal lookups are quick; multi-deal lists or valuation books take a few hours. Pulling standard documents and tracking status is the automatable share; explaining amounts stays manual.

processes.description: Risk keeps the list of Enovate/EMW and other trading books that must be officialized each night, since Credit picks up all officialized books. When a book is missed or the list is wrong, Darron Giron explains why the benchmark signoff did not catch it, updates the list and recirculates it, sometimes after misreading what was asked.
steps: A request arrives for the current list of books officialized each night.
The list of books is compiled and checked against the books in use.
Books are marked official so Credit and downstream users pick them up.
Missed books or errors are explained and the list is corrected and resent.

stalls.summary: The request for the book list was misread, so the list had to be redone and was sent late with an apology.
A mistake on a book slipped past the benchmark signoff procedure and needed an explanation afterwards.

automation.approach: Maintain the officialized book list as a controlled list in the risk system and run a nightly check that compares books marked official against that list, reporting any book left unofficialized before Credit picks them up.
automation.rationale: The failures are missed books and lists that drift out of date; a nightly checklist tied to a maintained book list catches misses before they reach downstream users.

processes.description: Schedulers and traders announce absences and name who covers for them, circulate weekend and holiday on-call schedules with cell and pager numbers, and send on-call notes after each weekend describing calls received and actions taken, such as gas control pages, meter problems reported by producers, and corrected confirms. Managers also arrange skeleton staff for holiday trading days and cover for affiliates.
steps: Someone announces an absence or a weekend or holiday that needs coverage.
A backup or on-call person is named, with contact numbers for the period.
The on-call schedule or contact sheet is updated and circulated.
The on-call person handles calls from gas control, pipelines and counterparties.
Actions taken are logged, including changed nominations or confirms.
On-call notes are sent to the team after the shift for follow-up.

stalls.summary: Coverage arranged in advance was not passed on, so the person expected to cover knew nothing about it.
On-call contact details go stale: a manager could not reach a staff member because the cell number on file no longer worked, and pager numbers need revised contact sheets.

contradictions.summary: A coverage message names only "Mary" as handling off-system nominations, which could mean either of two staff with that first name, so the owner of that coverage is unclear.

automation.approach: Keep one shared on-call calendar and contact sheet that each person updates when they will be out, with backups named per pipeline or desk, and use a fixed on-call notes form that captures each call, the counterparty, the meter or contract, and the action taken.
automation.rationale: Coverage notices and weekend notes are free-form and scattered; a standard notes form and a single contact sheet make handovers complete, keep numbers current and show who covers what.

work_estimate.rationale: Most rounds are absence notices with little work beyond naming a backup. Weekend on-call rounds add handling calls from gas control and producers, changing nominations or confirms, and writing up the call log, which runs longer. Updating schedules and contact sheets and the structure of the notes can be templated; handling calls cannot.
